_note: Lab-only reviewable judgments (Artwork Crop Lab V2, section 13). Made by looking at each master and reading the catalog lore; not canonical, not read by production. Environment ids and the archetype each belongs to come from docs/research/lists-cover-classification.json, which this file does not change. verdict: strong | acceptable | poor.

haunted-and-deathly.scene: Moonlit Gothic cemetery before a ruined manor, fog, weathered stones, slate blue.

cursed-graveyard.why: A crumbling cemetery with mossy crypts is literally the foreground.

desecrated-graveyard.why: Misty graveyard of the unquiet dead; fog and headstones are the picture.

possessed-abode.why: A dwelling with a presence: the manor facade reads as exactly that.

vampires-castle.why: Gothic and ominous, but the lore is a castle on a mountain pass with a ravine; the art has no heights.

castle-of-wails.why: A shattered watchtower; the ruined manor is the right mood, the wrong building.

abandoned-building.why: A cursed multistory building; a haunted manor is a fair stand-in.

haunted-city.why: Restless spirits and decay, but one house is not a city.

neverhome-corridors.why: Neverhome Manor is a manor; the lore is its interior, the art its exterior.

shatter-the-heart.why: The Manor's living heart: the house is right, the scene is inside it.

haunted-oratorium.why: A ruined hall of echoing minds; ruin and ghosts fit, a lecture hall does not appear.

forced-penance.why: Guilt left by the judged dead; the graves fit the theme, the place is not a cemetery.

deserted-moor.why: A lonely moor of curious plants and wolf howls: open rolling land, no graves, no manor.

haunted-mountain-pass.why: Steep cliffs, mountain rivers and tall trees; the art is flat ground and a building.

wispy-wasteland.why: Moors, swamps and wisps over open land; nothing in the art is open wasteland.

valley-of-death.why: The land beyond the Veil, souls travelling to rest; a mortal cemetery is the wrong plane.

realm-of-the-dead.why: Endless colorless still water; the art is solid, detailed ground.

bubblys-bottom.why: An abandoned carnival and a clown ghost; a Gothic manor would mislead.

empty-cliffside-village.why: A village behind a waterfall on a cliff face; there is no cliff or waterfall in the art.

forgotten-ruins.scene: Monumental sandstone temple consumed by a primordial forest; colossal roots, dark entrance, golden light, 3:2.

forgotten-temple-of-the-serpent.why: Overgrown ruins hiding new owners: this is that exact picture.

korathi-temple.why: An ancient temple with deadly guardians; the colossal statues and dark door fit (Shadow essence is absent).

ruined-castle.why: Disrepair and vines on a large structure; reads as a castle ruin more than as a temple, but the claim is true.

abandoned-grove.why: Nature reclaiming a druidic site; the forest is right, the masonry is more than a grove has.

ancient-city.why: An intact abandoned past civilization; a single temple front stands for the city.

ancient-power-conduit.why: A ruin of old knowledge and power; the architecture says old, the power is missing.

ruined-mage-tower.why: Remains of arcane study; ruined monumental stone, but no tower.

search-the-ruins.why: Searching a cursed city for loot; ruins to scavenge, but sunlit and lush rather than cursed.

mistfield-of-possibility.why: Mists through ruins; the shafts of light and ruins fit, the thick mists do not.

moon-kingdom.why: Luminous ruins of a forgotten kingdom; luminous is here sunlight, and the lunar part is missing.

lost-village.why: Stone foundations and rotting timbers, nothing monumental left; the art would promise a temple.

swamp-ruins.why: A ruin below a swamp's surface; the art is dry, high and golden.

mystic-ring.why: A circle of standing stones on open ground; no stone circle appears and there is no open sky.

titan-boneyard.why: Stony canyons of giant skeletons; there are no bones or canyon walls.

valley-of-automata.why: Colossal metal bodies and gearwork; entirely stone and vegetation here.

arcane-sanctums.scene: Arcane observatory and wizard tower on cliffs at sunset, celestial mechanism, bridges, waterfalls, warm windows.

archmages-tower.why: An impossibly tall tower resonating with power: the lit tower and orb are the picture.

eternal-observatory.why: A magical observatory; the celestial mechanism is its centerpiece (the art is pristine, the lore dilapidated).

tower-of-the-moon.why: A multi-level tower, but its moonlike facade and the Moonlit King are not here.

cosmological-clocktower.why: A tall tower with an intricate clock face; the orb stands in for the clock, the square 300 ft shaft does not.

magic-city.why: Opulent, ease-filled magic; a palatial arcane complex is a fair glimpse, though not a city.

arcanists-laboratory.why: An abandoned mage complex; the complex reads, its ruin and twisted experiments do not.

laboratory.why: Halls of a mad mage; the architecture hints at halls, nothing is monstrous.

alchemists-abandoned-workshop.why: A lightning-powered immortality workshop; a sunset sanctum on cliffs has no lightning and no workshop.

arcane-laboratory.why: Bubbling vials and half-finished creatures: an indoor bench, not a monumental exterior.

arcane-magic-shop.why: A shop front attached to a residence; a cliff-top megastructure promises far more.

feasts-and-revelry.scene: Grand banquet hall: chandeliers, crimson drapery, laid tables, warm gold light, vaulted architecture, polished floor.

masquerade-ball.why: A high-society gala in a grand hall; the room is right (masks absent, no guests).

masquerade-ball-atlas.why: The premier party of the season; this hall is the setting.

masquerade-party.why: A lavish party in a noble's manor; the interior matches.

grand-feast.why: Community feast overflowing with food and drink; the laid tables and fruit are in front.

divine-feast.why: A feast table set for giants; the feast fits, the scale of the table does not show.

the-commanders-dinner.why: A fine dinner in warm magical light; far smaller than the cathedral-sized hall, same mood.

upscale-casino.why: Dazzling wealth and opulence; no gaming tables, but the grandeur reads.

fairwell-casino.why: A casino at its chaotic height; only the glitter carries over.

local-festival.why: A week-long commoner festival; a palace interior is the wrong class and the wrong outdoors.

town-festival.why: A neighborhood turned festival with games; no street or daylight in the art.

city-festival.why: Carts flowing around a stone plaza; the art is a closed hall.

scorecard.lead: One landscape master per archetype, judged at the recommended crops. Provisional: crops are starting values, and the verdicts are mine, not yours.
